description: Composite figure of four panels of cellular-automaton (CA) simulation curves for low-alloy steel, all with True strain on the x-axis (0.2–0.9). (a) DRX fraction (y-axis 0.0–1.0, ticks 0.0/0.3/0.6/0.9) for a transient strain-rate drop 0.1 s^-1 → 0.01 s^-1 at 950 °C, drawn as two stacked sub-panels annotated "T: 950°C, ε1: 0.2" (top) and "ε1: 0.4" (bottom), banner "Variation(0.1s^-1-0.01s^-1)"; each has Total (solid blue), First stage (dashed orange) and Second stage (dashed green) curves. (b) DRX fraction for a temperature rise 950 °C → 1050 °C at 0.01 s^-1, sub-panels "ε: 0.01s^-1, ε1: 0.2" and "ε1: 0.4", banner "Variation(950°C-1050°C)". (c) Average dislocation density (y-axis ×10^13) for the strain-rate drop, three stacked sub-panels labelled "Matrix grains", "DRX grains, ε1: 0.2" and "DRX grains, ε1: 0.4"; matrix legend Constant(0.01s^-1), 0.1s^-1-0.01s^-1(0.2 strain), 0.1s^-1-0.01s^-1(0.4 strain); DRX-grain sub-panels show DRXGs_I (dashed orange) and DRXGs_II (dashed green). (d) same three-sub-panel layout for the temperature rise, matrix legend Constant(1050°C), 950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain), 950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain). In every panel the first-stage fraction peaks and decays while the second-stage fraction nucleates later and takes over; matrix dislocation density falls steeply after the transient, DRXGs_I curves peak then collapse, DRXGs_II rise later.

subfigures.description: Two stacked sub-plots of DRX fraction vs True strain (0.2–0.9, y 0.0–1.0) for a transient strain-rate drop 0.1 s^-1 → 0.01 s^-1 at 950 °C; top sub-panel ε1: 0.2, bottom ε1: 0.4. Three curves per sub-panel: Total (solid blue), First stage (dashed orange), Second stage (dashed green). In the ε1: 0.2 case the First stage curve peaks between the 0.3 and 0.6 gridlines near strain 0.33 and then decays, while Second stage starts near strain 0.3 and climbs to the top of the axis; in the ε1: 0.4 case Total and First stage stay low until strain ≈0.4, then jump steeply to the 0.9 gridline level.

Two stacked sub-plots of DRX fraction vs True strain for a temperature rise 950 °C → 1050 °C at ε: 0.01s^-1; top sub-panel ε1: 0.2, bottom ε1: 0.4. Same Total / First stage / Second stage colour scheme. At ε1: 0.2 the steep rise of Total occurs near strain 0.25–0.3 and First stage peaks near the 0.6 gridline around strain 0.3 before falling to near zero by strain 0.6; at ε1: 0.4 the steep rise occurs near strain 0.45–0.5.

Three stacked sub-plots of Average dislocation density (×10^13) vs True strain (0.2–0.9) for the strain-rate drop at 950 °C. Top: Matrix grains with legend Constant(0.01s^-1), 0.1s^-1-0.01s^-1(0.2 strain) and 0.1s^-1-0.01s^-1(0.4 strain); the 0.4-strain curve rises above the 10 gridline near strain 0.4 and then drops abruptly back to the level of the other curves. Middle: DRX grains ε1: 0.2 with DRXGs_I (dashed orange) peaking near the 2 gridline then roughly flat, DRXGs_II (dashed green) rising later to about 1.5. Bottom: DRX grains ε1: 0.4, DRXGs_I rising to a peak above the 4 gridline near strain 0.42 then collapsing, DRXGs_II rising after strain ≈0.45.

Three stacked sub-plots of Average dislocation density (×10^13) vs True strain for the temperature rise 950 °C → 1050 °C at ε: 0.01s^-1. Top: Matrix grains with legend Constant(1050°C), 950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain) and 950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain); both transient curves lie above the constant curve and decline steeply after strain ≈0.4 toward a common low level. Middle: DRX grains ε1: 0.2 with DRXGs_I peaking near the 0.9 gridline around strain 0.3 then decaying, DRXGs_II rising slowly. Bottom: DRX grains ε1: 0.4, DRXGs_I rising to a peak near the 2 gridline around strain 0.42 then dropping sharply to near zero, DRXGs_II rising after strain ≈0.5.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots DRX fraction (y-axis 0.0–1.0, ticks 0.0/0.3/0.6/0.9) against True strain (0.2–0.9) and contains three curves per sub-panel labelled Total (solid blue), First stage (dashed orange) and Second stage (dashed green).

In (a) top sub-panel (annotated 'T: 950°C', 'ε1: 0.2', banner 'Variation(0.1s^-1-0.01s^-1)') the First stage curve rises to a maximum between the 0.3 and 0.6 gridlines at strain ≈0.33 and then decays towards zero, while Second stage starts near strain 0.3 and climbs to the top of the axis by strain 0.9.
In (a) bottom sub-panel ('ε1: 0.4') the Total and First stage curves remain low until strain ≈0.4 then rise steeply to the 0.9 gridline level, and Second stage only begins after strain ≈0.45.

In (b) top sub-panel ('ε: 0.01s^-1', 'ε1: 0.2', banner 'Variation(950°C-1050°C)') the First stage DRX fraction peaks near the 0.6 gridline at strain ≈0.3 and falls to near zero by strain 0.6, whereas Second stage rises from strain ≈0.45 to the top of the axis.

Panel (c) is a three-sub-panel plot of Average dislocation density (×10^13) versus True strain, labelled from top to bottom 'Matrix grains', 'DRX grains' with ε1: 0.2, and 'DRX grains' with ε1: 0.4; the matrix legend is Constant(0.01s^-1), 0.1s^-1-0.01s^-1(0.2 strain) and 0.1s^-1-0.01s^-1(0.4 strain), and the DRX-grain sub-panels distinguish DRXGs_I (dashed orange) from DRXGs_II (dashed green).

In (c) the matrix curve for '0.1s^-1-0.01s^-1(0.4 strain)' rises to a value just above the 10 gridline near strain 0.4 and then drops abruptly to the level of the other matrix curves at strain ≈0.42, while the Constant(0.01s^-1) matrix curve declines smoothly from about the 4 gridline to about the 1 gridline.

In (c) bottom sub-panel (DRX grains, ε1: 0.4), DRXGs_I rises to a peak above the 4 gridline near strain 0.42 and then collapses to near zero by strain 0.45, while DRXGs_II stays near zero until ≈0.45 and then rises to roughly the 1.5 level.

Panel (d) repeats the three-sub-panel dislocation-density layout at ε: 0.01s^-1 for the 950 °C–1050 °C transient, with matrix legend Constant(1050°C), 950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain) and 950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain); both transient matrix curves lie above the constant 1050 °C curve and decay steeply after strain ≈0.4.

The caption states that (a) and (c) are the DRX-fraction and average-dislocation-density evolutions caused by transiently decreasing the strain rate from 0.1 s^-1 to 0.01 s^-1 at 0.2 or 0.4 strains at 950 °C, and that (b) and (d) are those caused by increasing temperature from 950 °C to 1050 °C in strain ranges of 0.2–0.3 or 0.4–0.5 at 0.01 s^-1.
The caption states the curves are simulated with CA models and give the evolutions of DRX fraction and average dislocation density resulting from DRXGs and DRXGs_II.

The citing text states that the DRX fraction of the first stage initially rose rapidly after a sudden decrease of Z_P and then declined gradually because of the refinement of DRXGs_II, as shown in Fig. 24a and 24b.

The citing text states that an increase in DRV caused by the Z_P drop results in a decline of the average dislocation density of the DRXGs and matrix in the initial part of the second stage, as illustrated in Fig. 24c and 24d.

The citing text states that DRX grain refinement additionally promoted a decrease in the average dislocation density of the matrix in Fig. 24c and 24d, producing a faster fall of flow stress to a level below that of the constant deformation condition.
No numerical data labels are printed on any curve; values can only be read qualitatively relative to the printed axis gridlines.

measured_quantities: average dislocation density (×10^13, unit not printed on axis)
unreadable_items: Panel letters are cropped at the top-left corner of each supplied image (only fragments such as 'b)' are visible), so the (a)-(d) assignment of each image was inferred from the caption text and the on-panel annotations rather than read directly
y-axis unit of 'Average dislocation density' is not printed - the label only gives the multiplier '(10^13)'
exact peak/trough values of individual curves are not printed and could not be read numerically
legend text in the lower sub-panels of (c) and (d) is small and only partially readable at the supplied resolution
